subject: CypherLytics POC — burst/reservation plan and onboarding next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Morales <ethan.morales@cypherlytics.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: POC goals + capacity questions

Hi Ethan — great to speak earlier. Quick recap and asks so we can size the trial properly: 

Summary of the call:
- Primary goal: validate real-time inference quality and latency for our Gen-2 retrieval-augmented chat flow against your 1.5M monthly active users (pilot cohort ~5k MAU).
- Success criteria (as discussed):
  * 95th pct latency for short chat requests (<= 512 tokens) < 300ms
  * End-to-end throughput to support 100 concurrent chat sessions during peak
  * Model output quality parity vs. your current baseline (we'll set an eval prompt set)

Capacity clarifications we need from your side by EOD Mon: 
1) Typical request distribution: RPS at baseline and peak (avg, p95, p99).  
2) Request payload sizes: average and 95th percentile token lengths for prompts and expected response length.
3) Any special preprocessing or multi-turn KV cache expectations (do you keep long-lived sessions?).

What we propose from Redwood (preliminary):
- Reserved baseline: 2 x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs dedicated to the trial (predictable throughput for steady-state).
- Autoscale/burst: allow bursting up to 6 GPUs for short windows (5–30 minutes) to absorb spikes; burst triggers and cooldowns configurable.
- KV prefix caching for warmed sessions to reduce token compute for returning users.

Next steps and owners:
- Ethan: please send the sample traffic profile and the eval prompt set (attach as CSV/JSON) and confirm SSO/SAML timeline.
- Camila (me): compile capacity ask and confirm reserved qty with infra.
- Vivek: will propose an exact GPU + autoscale configuration and cost delta by tomorrow.
- Aditya: will validate data ingress and encryption requirements with our onboarding runbook.

Attachments: cypher_poc_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), cypher_sample_payload.json (sample payload).

Thanks — looking forward to getting the trial scheduled.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0124

From: Ethan Morales <ethan.morales@cypherlytics.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@cypherlytics.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 17:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: POC goals + capacity questions

Camila — thanks for the clear recap. Attaching the dataset and a short traffic snapshot. Answers inline: 

1) Traffic: baseline ~12 RPS (aggregate across the pilot), peak bursts hit ~120 RPS for 3–7 minutes during our usage tests. Typical diurnal variation about 2x.
2) Payload sizes: prompt tokens avg ~180, p95 ~600; response tokens avg ~120. We use retrieval augmentation so some prompts can push to ~1k tokens occasionally.
3) Sessions: we keep session state for up to 30 minutes; typical conversation length 6–9 turns. We rely on warmed KV caches for returning sessions.

Acceptable acceptance criteria (we can be flexible):
- 95th pct latency < 400ms for single-turn, <=512 token flows; if you can get to <300ms wed be ecstatic.
- For burst windows, p95 can degrade to 600ms so long as throughput is maintained and there is no 5xx error rate > 0.2%.

I've attached the sample payload and a short CSV with per-minute RPS during our peak test. Also included an initial list of compliance questions in the security contact mailbox (security@cypherlytics.com).

Ethan
Ethan Morales
Head of Platform — CypherLytics
ethan.morales@cypherlytics.com
(650) 555-0189

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: POC goals + capacity questions

Thanks — read the payload and traffic snapshot. Proposal below (engineering/ops view):

Quick assumptions from the Cypher snapshot: baseline 12 RPS, short peak ~120 RPS, token lengths p95 ~600, sessions ~30 min. Using Redwood's throughput profiles for the family of LLMs they plan to run (seq len 700 average for round trips) we recommend: 

Option A (conservative, lower cost):
- Reserved: 2 x A100-80GB-equivalent (dedicated)
- Autoscale: allow burst to 4 GPUs for up to 30 minutes per 15-minute cooldown window
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~100 concurrent short chat sessions; p95 latency target ~350ms under steady bursts
- Cost estimate: incremental ~$8k/week for reserved + burst metering (estimated)

Option B (performance-first):
- Reserved: 4 x A100-80GB-equivalent
- Autoscale: burst to 8 GPUs with 10-minute minimum burst window and 30-minute cooldown
- Expected p95 latency <300ms for the sample traffic; handles sustained spikes more gracefully
- Cost estimate: incremental ~$18k/week

Operational notes:
- Burst triggers: we can wire burst on CPU-side queue length or an RPS threshold; recommend RPS>80 for initial rule.
- Warmup: recommend a 15–20 minute warmup with synthetic calls pre-roll to populate KV caches before the trial goes live to customers.
- Data plane: TLS in transit, customer-provided S3 for ingestion (Aditya to confirm buckets & encryption).

Timeline suggestion:
- Week 1 (May 2): Reserved capacity provisioned + SSO + runbook review.
- Week 2 (May 3–9): Warmup and smoke tests with synthetic traffic.
- Week 3 (May 10–16): Live pilot with selected cohort; concurrent monitoring and rolling adjustments.

Ill prepare a one-page SOW and the pricing delta for both options. If we get the sample eval prompts today we can run a short benchmark to sanity-check latencies.

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Infrastructure | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Recap: POC goals + capacity questions

Ethan — perfect, thanks for the fast turn. Vivek sent two options; summary below and a recommended next step.

Short summary for CypherLytics: 
- Option A (lower cost): 2 reserved GPUs, burst to 4; target steady p95 ~350ms; shorter warmup.
- Option B (performance-first): 4 reserved GPUs, burst to 8; target p95 <300ms for your sample profile.

Recommend we start with Option A for the initial two-week pilot (gives predictable cost and we can validate the eval prompts). If we see sustained high bursts during Week 1 we can convert to Option B quickly (Vivek says switching to more reserved GPUs is straightforward while trial is running).

Can you confirm: 
- We have approval to proceed with Option A starting May 2?
- Share the eval prompt CSV and confirm who on your side will be our security contact for SOC2 artifacts and the SSO owner.

Once you confirm, Ill kick off the provisioning ticket and share the onboarding runbook (link below).

Runbook link: https://redwood.example.com/runbooks/poc-burst-playbook

Thanks,
Camila
